paper.title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
paper.central_claim: Closed-loop natural-language feedback from success detection, scene description and human interaction enables pretrained LLM planners to reason, retry and replan for complex embodied tasks, significantly improving high-level instruction completion across simulated tabletop, real tabletop and real kitchen mobile manipulation, including disturbances and emergent interactive behaviors.
paper.central_claim_son55_wording: Feeding language-form environment feedback (success detection, passive object/scene description, active human/VQA answers) back into a frozen LLM planner over pretrained skills lets it retry, replan or ask, significantly improving instruction completion in simulated and real tabletop rearrangement and real kitchen mobile manipulation, especially under disturbances.

source_refs.embedded_text: - **E02 (ablation, common_practice).** Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions. — _applies when_ a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.

source_refs.embedded_text: - **E03 (ablation, common_practice).** Report the harness or tool effect under at least two backbones of different strength. Several read papers find that tools and imposed structure help weak models and are neutral or harmful for strong ones. A gain measured on the teacher therefore does not predict the gain for a compact student. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness component or tool helps in general, or that a teacher-measured tool value will carry to a student.

source_refs.embedded_text: - **E04 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Report run-to-run variance and use paired task-level statistics: repeated runs per setting, bootstrap or permutation CIs over tasks, and sign tests on discordant episodes. A single run on a 100-episode subset is treated as descriptive. In the read single-run papers, differences of a few points sit within noise. — _applies when_ any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.

claims.text: Closed-loop natural-language feedback from success detection, scene description and human interaction enables pretrained LLM planners to reason, retry and replan for complex embodied tasks, significantly improving high-level instruction completion across simulated tabletop, real tabletop and real kitchen mobile manipulation, including disturbances and emergent interactive behaviors.
claims.setting: Sim InstructGPT1.3B+scripted feedback; real tabletop InstructGPT1.3B+MDETR/heuristic; kitchen PaLM540B+SayCan+human objects.
claims.selection_vs_test: 4seen/4unseen sim behaviors with all-object primitive training; real tasks/scene substrate developed locally. No construction-unseen site split.
claims.result/denominator: 50sim episodes/task,cap15;10real tabletop runs/task,combined100%stacking/80%sorting,mean90% vsopen-loop20%; kitchen120evaluations,30.8→48.7→60.4%. Simulation matching bowls Object56→+Success70→+Scene82%,mismatched62→76→86%; difficult unseen corner stacking0→4→6%. These are not uniform success improvements on every task.
claims.counterevidence: Scene variant bundles chain-of-thought; oracle/human privilege in sim and kitchen Object; kitchen totals imply unequal per-method denominators and no CIs; real-tabletop noise protocol inconsistent between Sec 4.2 and Appendix A.2. CLIPort with a termination oracle exceeds every Inner Monologue variant on 3 of 4 seen simulated tasks (stack 32 vs <=26; corner/side 32 vs <=30; [x] bowl 94 vs <=56), while Inner Monologue wins pick-and-place (94 vs 74) and all unseen tasks.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Textual feedback improves measured robustness, with automated tabletop distinct from assisted kitchen; not fully autonomous general mobile manipulation or clean transfer.

assessment.author_claim_kept: Closed-loop natural-language feedback from success detection, scene description and human interaction enables pretrained LLM planners to reason, retry and replan for complex embodied tasks, significantly improving high-level instruction completion across simulated tabletop, real tabletop and real kitchen mobile manipulation, including disturbances and emergent interactive behaviors.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With textual success/scene feedback (ground-truth in sim, MDETR heuristics on a real tabletop, a learned detector plus human object labels in a real kitchen), a frozen LLM planner over pretrained skills recovers from induced failures better than the same planner without feedback (real tabletop 20% -> 90% over 2x10 runs; kitchen 30.8% -> 48.7% with learned success detection alone -> 60.4% with human object feedback). It does not uniformly beat a trained policy with a termination oracle on seen simulated tasks; emergent behaviours are anecdotal.
